en: I bow to the Goddess whose eyes are as long as lotuses, whose pair of feet is saluted by the hosts of the lords of gods; I bow to Durgā, the protector of all the exalted deities and the destroyer of misfortune. 1.

I bow to that Durgā, the sovereign of the gods, whose lotus feet are marked by the tips of crowns, who is as swift as thought, the consort of the Supreme Lord, and whose crown is adorned with a crescent moon.

I take refuge for the attainment of my desired goal in the Goddess who is full of bliss, whose palms are like the nectar-rayed moon, and who sits upon his lap—she who colors the quarters of space with her mass of ruddy luster; while he, the Lord of Teachers who awakens one to all the arts (kalās), is seated upon a divine, supreme lion-throne surrounded by the Great Deities of the threefold fundamental Śrī-Bhairava-nature.

I bow to Mahāśūlinī, who stands mounted upon the shoulder of the five-faced one, grasping with her two hands a terrible trident-weapon resembling millions upon millions of the fires at the end of an aeon; she who, through the various sounds of her diverse heroic sports—enveloped by the universe—subdues the entire multitude of all those petty enemies.

One should meditate upon the Supreme Mother, the Sovereign of All, who resembles a jasmine flower, the moon, and a conch shell; who sits upon a lion; who holds a bow, arrows, a skull, a book, a rosary, a trident, the gesture of granting boons, and the gesture of fearlessness; who pacifies the entire multitude of sins; who is intent on compassion for her devotees; and who is the sole granter of boons for the heart’s desires of the universe. 5.

One should meditate upon the Great Goddess who wields the Trident—she who is as dark and tender as a rain cloud, whose face is graced with a smile, and who sits upon a lion-throne; she who daily paralyzes the hosts of soldiers hostile to her devotees with waters falling from the Varuṇa-weapon drawn from the string of her bow, filling the eight directions, and who effects the dissolution of all forms in the universe.

Mounted upon a lion, holding in her hands a sword, a shield, a discus, a conch, a bow, a noose, a goad, and the gestures of fearlessness and granting boons—O Śūlinī, who brings victory, destroy the pride of all enemies before you and proceed incessantly for the prosperity of the universe! 7.

O Goddess who is the light of universal radiance, whose form consists of manifold manifestations, who dwells within the lotus-heart of the universe, who is uniquely skilled in teaching the world through various forms suited to its diverse activities—forgive all offenses against the universe, destroy every kind of evil instantly, protect us forever, O Sovereign of the Auspicious Trident-Bearer, and remain eternally present through Your innate compassion. 8.
